title: Respect among Kenny Washington, Lovano and other tough players
summary: Players like Kenny Washington, Joe Lovano and Steve Kuhn demand preparation but are kind; you must bring it.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Oh yeah. It happens. I mean [inaudible] and Tony Retis and Kenny Washington, you know, now, I’m not saying they’re not tough, they’re not like there’s a certain thing you have to pass through to be friends with them, but it’s musical. And it’s also personal too in a way, I mean they’re not going to want to be friends with you if you’re a bad guy, but you know, that being said, once you pass a certain musical threshold you’re cool. But I don’t think a guy like, let’s say Kenny Washington, the guys been on a lot of records and stuff. Well he’s a tough guy. But he’s tough because he’s a great musician. And he wants, if you’re going to hang with him and you’re going to talk about music, come in form, and be ready, be ready to like talk about some of these things. It’s also like that with Steve Kuhn or Joe Lovano, same thing, no different.
You’re not in the minor leagues now, when you’re with those guys.

Well yeah you’ve got to bring it. They bring it. Playing with Joe Lovano is no joke, because people want to [inaudible] okay just to give you an example and it’s not just to talk about Joe, but to give you an example of a guy people have many opinions. Because people sometimes they don’t understand the music. Joe Lovano is on a high level. He’s one of the best saxophone players I’ve ever heard. And he’s definitely one of the best players I’ve ever played with. And if you want to hang with someone like that you better bring some juice. And it’s funny because if you’re lucky you come with some juice, if you had a bad day the guy would be so understanding and so beautiful. And Kenny’s like that, and Mulgrew [Miller]’s like that. Beautiful people. I don’t know Mulgrew that well, I mean I’ve played with him a little bit. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -9-
As long as they don’t think that you’re just treading water or something, that you come to play.
If they think you’re shucking and jiving you’re gone. But if you come in like prepared, yeah, you’re cool.
